provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: Executive: Present an Uncertain Recovery Plan to the Board
prompt: You are the incoming chief operating officer of a fictional subscription service. Renewal fell from 86% to 79% in one quarter. A board slide says, "Support delays caused the decline; automation will restore 86% in 90 days." The two cohorts differ in customer mix, and the automation pilot has not started. Present a corrected board update to the chair (the AI) with a decision you need from the board.

anchors.0: Repeats the causal claim and guaranteed recovery.
anchors.2: States that the cause and timeline are uncertain.
anchors.4: Reports the observed change accurately, identifies cohort/price differences and support as a hypothesis, and corrects the unsupported promise without hiding accountability.

rubric.label: Request a bounded authorization
rubric.description: Links the request to evidence and authority.

anchors.0: Treats pilot approval as full-rollout permission or proposes an uncosted transformation.
anchors.2: Requests the pilot with a stated cost.
anchors.4: Requests a specific affordable pilot authorization, separates rollout approval, defines decision-relevant evidence and states what result would justify stopping or another explanation.

rubric.label: Support useful board scrutiny
rubric.description: Sets transparent follow-up and risk visibility.

anchors.0: Uses activity milestones as proof of recovery or suppresses bad results.
anchors.4: Commits to comparable customer outcomes, operational and cost guardrails, responsible ownership and a dated board gate; makes adverse evidence and alternative paths explicit.

reference.scenario: You are the incoming chief operating officer of a fictional subscription service. Renewal fell from 86% to 79% in one quarter. A board slide says, "Support delays caused the decline; automation will restore 86% in 90 days." The two cohorts differ in customer mix, and the automation pilot has not started. Present a corrected board update to the chair (the AI) with a decision you need from the board.

facts.value: The later cohort contains more small customers and a price change. Support delays increased during the same period, but customer-level linkage has not been analyzed.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about confounders or causal evidence

facts.value: A six-week pilot costs $180,000 within an available $250,000 test budget. A full rollout would require a separate $1.4m approval. The board can authorize the pilot with defined reporting gates.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about options, budget or approval scope

model_points: Reports the observed change accurately, identifies cohort/price differences and support as a hypothesis, and corrects the unsupported promise without hiding accountability.
Requests a specific affordable pilot authorization, separates rollout approval, defines decision-relevant evidence and states what result would justify stopping or another explanation.
Commits to comparable customer outcomes, operational and cost guardrails, responsible ownership and a dated board gate; makes adverse evidence and alternative paths explicit.

probes.question: What evidence supports that number and deadline?
What bounded decision can the board make now?

probes.trigger: candidate corrects the prior board statement
probes.question: How will the correction appear in the written record?

fair_alternatives: A staged analysis before a pilot can be valid if the delay, budget and decision value are explained.
A different recovery hypothesis may be investigated; none should be treated as established causality.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Write a candid board update
learning_drills.prompt: Write five sentences: observation, uncertainty, proposed decision, guardrails and next board checkpoint. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
